newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade quiet.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were mostly stable in late trading on Friday, with declines in Malaysia keeping demand thin and sentiment weak, traders said.

They said palm olein was generally quoted at 1,370-75 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, but trades were also heard at five rupiah below and above the range. Crude palm oil was offered at around the last tender price of 1,175 rupiah/kg in Medan.

"The market is drifting, with declines in Malaysia keeping buyers mostly sidelined," one trader said. "They are not keen on taking fresh positions because of volatility in Malaysia, and would rather buy in small quantities regularly."
The traders said they expected prices to remain soft next week on sustained poor buying interest, adding that a sharp fall in Chicago soyoil futures on Thursday could weigh on prices.
Soyoil prices fell to a 3-1/2-year low on the back of large supplies and weak demand in export markets.
"I think it will weigh on the market," one trader said.
Data from Belawan port showed that the M.T. Bukit-I will leave the North Sumatran port on Saturday with 1,000 tonnes of palm olein for Tanjung Priok in Jakarta.
